Explosion · Romania

Romania says Russian drone’s payload detonated mid-air before Solca crash

24 September 2026 · Solca

Russian-attributed cross-border incursion; reported airborne explosion and crash

On 24 September 2026 a small drone crossed from Ukraine into Romanian airspace over northern Botoșani and crashed in woodland near Solca, in Suceava County, after about four minutes in Romanian airspace; military radar confirmed the entry. Minister Miruță said its explosive load separated shortly before the crash and detonated in the air. Residents located and filmed the wreckage.

Miruță described a Russian-model drone with equipment Romanian specialists had not encountered before. The Institute for the Study of War identified the wreckage from geolocated imagery as a Russian Gerbera-type drone; that is ISW’s assessment, not an official Romanian model identification. Lithuania’s Foreign Ministry attributed the wider 24 September incursions into Romania and Moldova to Russian drones. The launching unit, intended target and cause of the incursion remain unresolved.

Two Romanian F-16s took off from Borcea to monitor the drone, and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter launched from Bacău at 07:21. Miruță said the conditions for engaging it were not met; it was not shot down. Interior Ministry teams secured the site. No casualties or material damage were reported, and there was no fire at the crash site.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
Russian — high confidence, based on official attribution and corroborating assessment. Miruță described a Russian-model drone; ISW identified Russian Gerbera-type wreckage at Solca. Lithuania’s Foreign Ministry attributed the broader 24 September Romanian and Moldovan incursions to Russian drones.
Investigation / uncertainty
Event and cross-border entry: very high confidence (official/radar-confirmed). Russian attribution: high confidence. Gerbera-type remains an ISW assessment, not an official Romanian model identification. Exact operating unit, intended target and cause of the incursion remain unresolved. Lithuania’s statement corroborates the broader incursions, not Solca-specific forensic details.
